question: Which Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub is shipped: the C/GTK track, the Rust/GTK track, a different scoped architecture, or deferral into narrower follow-ups?
rationale: Current main solves Windows availability but Linux remains a broad desktop product, security, packaging, and ownership decision with multiple open implementation candidates.

options.title: Choose one Linux track
options.body: Select the supported Linux companion architecture, close or redirect alternatives, and require current gateway-contract, packaging, security, and runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue for platform status while creating narrower issues for Linux tray, setup, chat, node capabilities, packaging, and docs so work can land incrementally.

options.title: Defer Linux app work
options.body: Explicitly keep Gateway-only Linux support for now and close or pause implementation PRs until security and ownership bandwidth exists.

recommendation.title: Choose one Linux track
recommendation.body: Select the supported Linux companion architecture, close or redirect alternatives, and require current gateway-contract, packaging, security, and runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the platform request and provided the clearest product-direction comments in the issue discussion.
